title: Enterprise Onboarding & Support Playbook — Onboarding, Escalation, Integration, QBRs
author: Asha Patel
content:
Summary

This playbook consolidates Redwood Inference's enterprise onboarding and support processes for self-serve and sales-assisted customers. It includes: a repeatable onboarding timeline, integration checklist, escalation paths, support SLAs/SLOs, known issues & workarounds, and a QBR / health-check template. Use this as the canonical reference for Customer Success (CS), Solutions Engineering (SE), Support, and On-call SRE during the first 90 days of customer engagement.

Audience
- Customer Success Managers (CSMs)
- Solutions Engineers (SEs)
- Technical Support Engineers
- On-call SREs and Infra teams
- Product and Account owners during QBRs

Ownership
- Playbook owner: Customer Success (Asha Patel)
- Escalation coordination: Support (Michael Chen)
- Integration templates and API details: Eng Developer Experience

Scope
This document covers: enterprise onboarding flows for Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments; integration prerequisites; escalation matrix and procedures; standard SLOs for support; common known issues and mitigations; and a QBR/health-check template. It does NOT replace product-specific runbooks or customer-specific contract terms (refer to linked contract and SLA).

Prerequisites (pre-contract / pre-kickoff)
- Signed order form and security addendum (if required).
- Technical contact list (names, emails, pager/phone, Slack handles).
- Target environments and compliance requirements (VPC, region, data residency).
- High-level architecture diagram (customer side) and example traffic profile.

Pre-onboarding checklist (to complete before Kickoff meeting)
1. Create customer workspace in Redwood Console and assign CSM and SE.
2. Provision a test API key (scoped) and an admin key for SE.
3. Validate account entitlements (models, embedding units, Dedicated capacity if purchased).
4. Prepare onboarding playbook packet (this doc + integration checklist + sample prompts/evals).
5. Schedule initial Kickoff (Week 0) and invite SRE/Network where Private/Dedicated applies.

High-level 12-week onboarding timeline
- Week 0 (Kickoff):
  - Introductions, scope, success metrics, communication channels (Slack + Jira).
  - Review security and network requirements for Dedicated/Private.
  - Agree on P0/P1 definitions and escalation expectations.

- Week 1-9: Initial integration and smoke tests:
  - Provide sample curl/SDK calls, example prompts, and baseline eval suite.
  - SE validates token usage, rate-limits, and request/response shapes.
  - For Dedicated/Private: validate VPC peering, subnets, and NAT/egress rules.

- Week 2-9: Performance and scale validation:
  - Run throughput and latency tests (see 'Perf acceptance criteria' below).
  - Configure batching/caching settings; capture token cost baseline.
  - Set up dashboard access for customer (Console + read-only Grafana where applicable).

- Week 4: User acceptance and rollout plan:
  - Finalize canary rollout plan and fallback model variants.
  - Create runbook for cutover and rollback.
  - Sign-off from product owners and security.

- Weeks 4 to 12: Stabilization and optimization
  - Monitor production traffic, tune batching/quantization profiles, and update cost/quality tradeoffs.
  - Schedule QBR at Week 8 and Week 12 for enterprise customers.

Integration guide (developer-facing quickstart)
1) API keys and auth
  - Generate scoped API key in Console > API Keys. Use separate keys per environment (dev/staging/prod).
  - Example curl (text generation):
    curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood-inference.example/v1/generate \
      -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" \
      -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
      -d '{\"model\":\"redwood-alpha-3b\",\"input\":\"Translate to French: Hello\"}'

2) Network requirements (Dedicated / Private)
  - Egress: allow outbound to the Redwood control plane: control.redwood.ai:443 (TLS).
  - For Private deployments: customer must provide CIDR for management plane and allow inbound from assigned management IPs.
  - Ports: 443 (HTTPS), and customer-specified ports for metrics/ops (documented in deployment ticket).

3) Observability and access
  - Grant customer read-only Console access; grant support and SRE service accounts appropriate roles.
  - Provide Grafana dashboard link + sample metrics (latency p50/p95, tokens/sec, error rate, cache hit rate).

4) Prompts, evals and quality guardrails
  - Provide baseline prompt set (up to 10 representative prompts). Run Redwood eval harness (applied-ml-and-evals/eval-harness) and capture pass/fail metrics.

Performance acceptance criteria (example)
- Cold-start 95th percentile latency: <= 800 ms for text generation at 256 tokens (hosted small instance profile).
- Sustained throughput: handles customer peak expected QPS with <1% 5xx errors.
- Token cost: within 20% of pre-agreed cost estimate (post-quantization/ batching).

Escalation playbook (operational steps + contacts)
Severity definitions:
- P1 (Critical/outage): Customer production traffic is disrupted for all users or major SLA breach. Immediate mitigation required.
- P2 (High): Major feature degraded impacting many users; workaround exists.
- P3 (Medium): Single-customer or minor issue; limited business impact.
- P4 (Low): Enhancement request or minor cosmetic issue.

Escalation matrix (primary):
- P1:
  - Step 1: Customer reports via support portal or pager; CSM opens incident ticket.
  - Step 2: Triage by Support L1 within 15 minutes; escalate to Support L2/SRE if not resolved in 30 minutes.
  - Step 3: Notify oncall-sre (Slack #oncall-sre) and post to incident bridge.
  - Target response time: 15 minutes; target mitigation (temporary fix/rollback) within 1 hour.

- P2:
  - Target initial response: 1 hour; resolution or targeted mitigation in 4 business hours.

Contact & notification list (roles & channels)
- CSM (primary): Asha Patel — Slack: @asha.patel — Email: asha.patel@redwood.ai
- Support lead: Michael Chen — Slack: @mchen-support — Pager: +1-555-0102
- On-call SRE: see #oncall-sre channel roster (link in runbook).
- SE (integration): Priya Singh — Slack: @priya.se — Email: priya.singh@redwood.ai

Escalation communication templates
- Slack incident post: include title, severity, affected customer, brief impact, time, steps already taken, and link to ticket.
- Incident bridge agenda: 1) Summary 2) Impact 3) Current mitigation 4) Next actions 5) Owner assignments.

Support process, SLAs and SLOs
- Support channels: Support portal (preferred), support@redwood.ai, Enterprise Slack (invited), phone/pager for P1 only.
- Ticket triage: L1 acknowledges within SLA window, L2 assigns where required.
- Response time targets (SLA for enterprise customers):
  - P1: 15 minute response; continuous communication every 30 minutes until mitigation.
  - P2: 1 hour initial response; updates every 2 hours until resolved.
  - P3: 4 business hours initial response.
  - P4: 2 business days response.
- Resolution SLA: depends on contract; default internal SLOs are P1 resolved within 8 hours, P2 within 24 hours, P3 within 5 business days.

Escalation acceptance criteria & routing rules
- If incident impacts production traffic or causes data loss => escalate to P1.
- If error rate across >=5% of customer requests for 5 consecutive minutes => auto-alert and open P2 ticket.
- Route telemetry-based incidents via PagerDuty alerts to oncall SRE; route account-specific integration issues to SE/CSM first.

Known issues and workarounds (living table)
- Issue: Intermittent 503 from model-hosting during autoscaling
  - Symptom: 5xx spikes correlated with cold-start windows.
  - Workaround: Increase min-instances or enable warm-pool for critical routes; temporarily route traffic to fallback model variant.
  - Owner: Eng-serving-runtime

- Issue: Embedding index mismatch after model upgrade
  - Symptom: Retrieval quality drop after model change.
  - Workaround: Re-index embeddings using recommended quantization profile; pin older model for read path during re-index.
  - Owner: Applied ML and SE

- Issue: Private deployment control-plane unreachable behind restrictive NAT
  - Symptom: Management API timeouts and failure to receive patches.
  - Workaround: Validate egress rules to control.redwood.ai:443 and allow configured management IPs; temporary VPN tunnel possible.
  - Owner: Eng-private-deployments

- Issue: Increased token unit cost after enabling aggressive batching
  - Symptom: Lower latency but higher per-request token usage due to prompt duplication.
  - Workaround: Use prefix caching and dedup prompts at client side; re-evaluate batching window.
  - Owner: Eng-platform / Redwood Optimize

Health checks & QBR template
- Frequency: Week 8 and Week 12 QBRs for new enterprise customers; quarterly thereafter.
- Attendees: CSM, SE, Customer Product/Engineering, Support lead, SRE representative.

QBR agenda (60 minutes):
  1) Executive summary and business goals (5m)
  2) Usage and cost trends (10m) — tokens/month, avg tokens/req, cost per 1k tokens
  3) Performance and reliability (10m) — latency p50/p95, error rates, incidents since last meeting
  4) Quality and accuracy (10m) — eval pass rates, sample outputs, regression alerts
  5) Roadmap and feature requests (10m)
  6) Action items and responsibilities (10m)

Standard QBR metrics (examples)
- Tokens consumed (monthly)
- Avg / request tokens and token cost per 1k tokens
- Latency p50/p95 for typical request profiles
- 5xx error rate and incidents by severity
- Model quality metrics from eval harness (accuracy / hallucination rate)
- Cache hit rate and batching efficiency improvements

Rollout & cutover checklist
- Finalize rollback plan and smoke tests.
- Schedule maintenance window if required (document customer-visible downtime).
- Verify observability (alerts, dashboards) are enabled and accessible.
- Confirm SE and SRE on-call coverage for first 48 hours post-cutover.

RACI (high-level)
- CSM: Responsible for customer communication, success metrics, and QBRs.
- SE: Responsible for integration, performance tuning, and technical sign-off.
- Support: Responsible for triage, first-response, and incident coordination.
- SRE: Responsible for production incidents, scaling, and runbook execution.

Customer-facing templates
- Support request template (include in ticket):
  - Customer name, product environment (prod/staging), API key (masked), time window, sample request/response, steps to reproduce, recent deployments, log snippets, and priority/severity.

- Post-incident summary template:
  - Incident summary, timeline, root cause, mitigation steps, ongoing mitigations, follow-up actions, and owner for each action.

FAQ (common questions)
- Q: How do I request dedicated capacity?
  - A: Contact your CSM; we will open a Dedicated capacity request, map expected QPS, and share estimated lead time (usually 4-8 weeks depending on region).

- Q: Who can request model onboarding?
  - A: SE with Applied-ML and Product approval; submit model-onboarding ticket via internal intake form.

Review cadence
- This playbook is reviewed quarterly by Customer Success and Support leads. Major updates must include reviewers and be communicated in CS monthly sync.
